about: The Genobi teaser's brief and every owner correction, as project memory an agent records with `genobi decision` (source interpretation, quoting the owner) and the reusable rules as Taste proposals the owner activates. Apply with scripts/seed-genobi-teaser-memory.mjs; see docs/genobi-teaser.md#how-to-repeat-it.

decisions.value: Owner, 30 Oct 2026: "make the teaser video with Genobi usage and the music we have"; built like the Dimensions mix, "going through functions, so the agent can actually show stuff: zoom in, click, use effects, loaders, cool interface", with Transitions.dev transitions and our own Signal recipes.

Review of cut 1: no line may claim provenance it cannot back. The creature clips are the owner's MiniMax H3 outputs and the forest guardian a FLUX 3 run, made outside this cut; say what the studio did ("cut in Genobi"), never "made in the studio", and name only the models the piece used, such as MiniMax H3 (open weights).
Review of cut 1: the Scrolls page is light and jumps out of the dark look; keep it short (four beats) and zoomed onto its dark cells or dialogs.
Review of cut 1: UI text is tiny at 720p; every UI beat zooms onto a readable detail and holds it at least about 1.3 s (2 to 3 beats at 135 BPM).
Review of cut 1: the 3D shots showed a bare default room; use richer presets and a camera move.
Owner, round 2: "a bit blurry, too low res" and "internal looks lower res"; render 1920 × 1080 and record the studio at 2× (3840 × 2160) so a camera move keeps native detail. No AI upscale.
Owner, round 2: "Record as before, those were great actual takes"; re-record by replaying the same actions, timings and clicks (scripts/genobi-teaser-shots.mjs), only the resolution changes.
Owner, round 2, at about 1:14: "just paper shaders there, some of the shaders in the same colours, maybe a glittering shader"; Paper Shaders in Signal lime and lilac, on the composition clock.

Owner, round 2: a TASTE LAYER section on black listing the libraries Genobi really ships and credits (docs/credits/libraries), Transitions.dev and Paper Shaders included, typed in with a text effect; it also breaks up repetition.
Owner, round 2: less repetitive overall; tighten repeated beats and leave room for one more video of the owner's own (the project stays under 128 layers).
Owner, round 2: "we don't say about camera control, which is kind of a BFL thing"; at 0:27 type "camera controls" in the title style over Camera's camera controls (BFL's camera terms).
Owner, round 2: the vocal sings "Three.js"; at 0:36 a "★ Three.js" callout in the GENOBI title style, flowing straight into the ComfyUI workflow at 0:38: "show the workflow and zoom into it".

Owner, round 2: "at 0:38, inside the Comfy part, show the ComfyUI workflow we have, it's a Comfy competition, it's on brand"; Genobi's World Builder nodes in a ComfyUI started only for the capture, prompts never queued.

Owner, round 3: the shaders appear when the vocal sings "shaders, transitions" (around 1:17), and the following beats follow the words: transitions, creative references with credit, licence information in view, run locally / open-weight / APIs, save the project, reuse the flow.

Owner, round 3: open the shader beat with Paper's dithering shader, lighter, in the teaser palette, with no big "PAPER SHADERS" title; then a Space.js effect right after, for variety instead of another typed title.
Owner, round 3: no text over the ComfyUI shot; the canvas speaks for itself.
Owner, round 3: ANDREW ZELLINGER first in the TASTE LAYER list; a second collaborator stays off screen until the owner confirms the name.
Owner, round 3: the typography is razor sharp, the generation clips softer; the owner upscales the FLUX and MiniMax clips himself and they are swapped in as files (UPSCALED in genobi-teaser.ts).

Owner, v3 review: "the recordings should be made in higher quality initially, and use the new cards; all the animations, all the pace, everything is fine — they should be made exactly the same, but recorded in higher resolution." Replay the same takes at 3840 × 2160, near-lossless, from the branch being cut.

Owner, v3 review: at about 1:20 remove the sudden character change; carry the same character into the pixel/dither transition instead of a hard switch, and keep the TASTE LAYER on a steady background with the line "Libraries, shaders, transitions and creative references — we credit the people who made them; shape that selection around your work."

Owner, v3 review: "for slice it can use the cut tool in the timeline — it's in the beginning as well — will work well, adjusting clip length in the timeline"; "around 0:19–0:20 — move a clip, adjust timing — that's where we can do it; it shows the FLUX selection instead, it can do that later"; "to 0:24 — send it back, can press the Regenerate button."

Owner, v3 review: "once it's talking about the space… it says change to cathedral or whatever space, but it's showing a different part of the app instead. It should show the 3D part in that space… and then show a default view of the 3D"; show the scene view, the 3D viewport filling the shot, default view first, then the Cathedral. Not yet placed: the beat needs the owner's timestamp.

taste.value: Say what the studio did, never where an external clip came from; no tool or provider named that the piece did not use.
Zoom every interface beat onto one readable detail and hold it at least 1.3 s; keep light pages short in a dark film.
Record interface footage at 2× the render (3840 × 2160 for 1080p) by replaying a scripted take; render at 1920 × 1080; no AI upscale.
Bundled fonts only (Instrument Sans, IBM Plex Mono, Pixelify Sans, Nokia Cellphone FC); free Transitions.dev transitions only, run unchanged.
